nodes.description: Two damaged copies of TEFM. The founding alleles are four missense variants (p.Arg34Trp, p.Pro157Ala, p.Ile159Lys, p.Lys188Arg), an in-frame two-residue deletion (p.Glu162_Arg163del), a frameshift, and a splice variant that causes exon 2 skipping and a second frameshift (p.Glu11Glyfs*2). Most missense changes cluster in the linker subdomain. Recombinant mutant proteins stimulated POLRMT processivity less than wild type, and TEFM protein was reduced in patient fibroblasts carrying p.Pro157Ala or p.Ile159Lys. All tested alleles kept residual activity, and no homozygous loss-of-function variant is seen in gnomAD.

nodes.description: Some patients have fluctuating, fatigable weakness with a decremental response on slow repetitive nerve stimulation, the picture of a congenital myasthenic syndrome. TEFM is now listed among congenital myasthenic syndrome genes. One later patient with the same fatigable picture had a normal repetitive stimulation test.

nodes.description: Brain involvement ranges from none on imaging to cortical and white matter loss, cerebellar atrophy and thin corpus callosum. The founding authors read the diversity of brain and muscle findings as showing that mitochondrial transcription elongation matters for many neuronal populations. No study has measured transcription or respiratory chain function in patient neurons, so this node rests on the clinical picture and the analogy with POLRMT disease.
